main_body: A T-shaped timber post: a thin vertical pole (rows 18-47) under a horizontal crossbeam (rows 9-17). The pole is the largest volume.
top_band: The crossbeam has an orange band at rows 9-12 with a cream line at row 13. The pole's column has no top band: it starts as a flat tan strip with a dark left edge and a dark right side strip. The base at rows 45-47 is just a dark cap.
evidence: Only the crossbeam reads as a top (about 4 rows), then a cream edge line and a brown face of about 4 rows. The vertical pole and the base are drawn straight on from the front, with no visible horizontal surface at the pole's top or at its foot. The frame contract requires its beams and base to show top faces, and the main body (the pole) is a flat front-view strip. The 2-3px dark strip on the right of the pole reads as a shadow, not a receding top. Strictly, this is a front elevation.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark brown tinted to the wood, which is acceptable. The beam has some dotted grain and a cream highlight. The pole is a narrow strip of 2-3 tones with little grain. Next to the stall and well references, which have 5-6 steps and many details per tile, this piece is far thinner and simpler, with low colour count per tile.
